newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU grain crop seen at 197.29 mln T. [CORRECTED 14:53 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU grain crop seen at 197.29 mln T. [CORRECTED 14:53 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects figures in the story as they were based on a June 27 forecast sent in error by Coceral.)
European Union grain output in the 15 member states is expected to fall to 197.29 million tonnes in 1997, from 201.54 million in 1996, Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby, forecast on Friday.

It saw the soft wheat crop falling to 88.43 million tonnes, from 90.57 million in 1996, and the barley crop falling to 50.84 million tonnes, from 51.84 million. The forecast, presented to the EU cereals advisory committee, saw durum wheat down at 6.77 million tonnes, from 7.19 million in 1996.
Maize output was seen marginally lower at 33.37 million tonnes, against 33.92 million in 1996.
Rye output was seen falling to 5.64 million tonnes, from 5.85 million tonnes last year.

The total grain crop forecast was based on a 4.7 percent fall in average yields to 5.28 tonnes per hectare, from 5.54 tonnes per ha in 1996, and a 2.7 percent area increase to 37.36 milllion ha from 36.36 million.
